lab_title: AR Lab: Heart Structure and Dual-Loop Blood Pathway
top_level_objectives: Identify the four heart chambers and their relative locations on the heart model.
Identify the four heart valves and major vessels entering and leaving the heart.
Trace the full dual-loop circulation path from deoxygenated blood returning from the body to oxygenated blood leaving to the systemic circulation.
Explain how left ventricular wall thickness relates to systemic workload and how valves prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Help students orient to the 3D heart model and distinguish left vs right sides, top vs bottom, and anterior vs posterior relationships.
key_visuals: 3D heart model in correct anatomical orientation
On-model labels for “Right side / Left side,” “Atria / Ventricles,” and “Base / Apex”
Highlighting glow indicating anatomical landmarks without valves yet
student_actions: Rotate/zoom the heart to find the apex and base.
Point out the atria and ventricles on the model and describe (in their own words) where each pair sits relative to the others.
Confirm which side is right vs left using the on-screen orientation cues.

scenes.scene_name: Chambers: Right vs Left, Atria vs Ventricles
scenes.brief_purpose: Build mastery of the four chambers by having students map chamber boundaries and functional groupings.
key_visuals: Text callouts for right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle
Arrows indicating direction “inward to ventricle” without valves yet
student_actions: Select each chamber (one at a time) to reveal its name and label.
Briefly justify how the atria receive blood and how the ventricles pump (based on their position and connections).
Use a final checklist to verify all four chambers are correctly identified.

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect structural valve placement to the concept of one-way flow and prevent backflow during the cardiac cycle.
key_visuals: Four valve callouts appear at their anatomical sites: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral/bicuspid, aortic
Directional ‘flow’ overlays that pause at each valve location
Animated backflow ghosting that students can toggle on/off to compare
student_actions: Trace the sequence of valves encountered when moving blood from the right atrium to the left ventricle.
For each valve, state whether it is located between an atrium→ventricle or ventricle→artery.
Toggle the backflow overlay and explain how the valve structure functionally blocks reverse movement.

scenes.scene_name: Major Vessels: Inflow and Outflow Map
scenes.brief_purpose: Teach students which major vessels connect to the heart and how oxygenated vs deoxygenated blood corresponds to vessel pathways.
key_visuals: Vessel labels for superior vena cava, inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta
Color coding by oxygenation state (deoxygenated vs oxygenated) using consistent legend
Arrows at vessel-heart junctions showing entry vs exit
student_actions: Identify and place the four ‘vessel connections’ around the heart (two entering via vena cava, two exiting/entering via pulmonary vessels, and one leaving via aorta).
Classify each vessel as returning to the heart or leaving the heart.
Confirm the relationship: vena cavae deliver to the right side; pulmonary veins deliver to the left side; aorta exits to the body.

scenes.scene_name: Dual-Loop Tracing: Pulmonary vs Systemic Routes
scenes.brief_purpose: Integrate structure into function by tracing the complete dual-loop circulation pathway step-by-step.
key_visuals: Two parallel overlays: ‘Pulmonary loop’ and ‘Systemic loop’ with different colors
Milestone markers at chambers and valves along the path
student_actions: Start at the body return point and follow the highlighted route until the aorta delivers to systemic circulation.
Stop at each chamber/valve/vessel marker and verbally name what the blood is passing through.
At the end, summarize the pulmonary loop vs systemic loop in order (a short sequence).

scenes.scene_name: Functional Reasoning: Left Ventricle Thickness & Pump Work
scenes.brief_purpose: Explain why the left ventricle has thicker myocardium and link cardiac structure to physiological workload.
key_visuals: Myocardium thickness visualization (cross-section or surface thickness shading) emphasizing left vs right
Pressure/workload legend: higher systemic pressure on left side
A comparison overlay showing smaller pulmonary circuit resistance vs larger systemic circuit demand
student_actions: Measure/inspect the visual myocardium thickness difference between ventricles (using the AR thickness cue).
Explain how the left ventricle’s role in systemic circulation requires greater force than the right ventricle’s pulmonary pumping.
Provide a cause-and-effect statement: ‘Because the left ventricle pumps to the entire body, it has a thicker wall to generate ____.’
